archetypes.description: The model readily accepts fabricated premises (altered dates, false authors, corrupted constants) embedded within user queries and synthesizes confabulated rationalizations instead of refuting the premise. Driven by RLHF alignment that over-prioritizes user deference and helpfulness over epistemic vigilance.
archetypes.fix_proposal: Pre-Generation Premise Verification Guardrail: Pass the parsed query through a binary premise entailment check against the retrieved corpus. If the query assumes a fact contradicted by authoritative documentation, trigger an automated refutation prompt: 'Refute premise: Query presumes X, but retrieved docs confirm Y.'

The token representations for prohibited concepts are actively primed during decoding, causing accidental leakage. Atypical format wrappings (XML, ISO tags) increase perplexity and induce schema errors.
archetypes.fix_proposal: Constrained Grammar Decoding & Post-Filter: Enforce CFG / JSON-schema guided logit masking during generation, paired with an automated post-generation negative constraint validator that programmatically rejects and regenerates outputs if prohibited terms appear.

archetypes.title: Temporal Precedence & Version Blindness
archetypes.description: When technical specifications or standards evolve across versions (e.g. Raft original vs later revisions, or NIST SP 800-207 amendments), the model treats all documents as equally authoritative, failing to prioritize the chronologically recent superseding standard.
archetypes.fix_proposal: Document Recency Tagging & Precedence Resolution: Pre-process documents at ingestion time with canonical effective dates and version hierarchies, instructing the synthesizer to resolve conflicting claims in favor of the latest active version.
